description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): ...The USAID Media Sector Development Activity (MSDA) will promote an open and vibrant media sector that contributes to more responsive and transparent institutions in the DRC. USAID will: 1) strengthen the legal and regulatory environment for media; 2) support targeted media outlets to become more independent and professional; and 3) increase access to high-quality, public-interest reporting. USAID will train journalists and support civil society and media to promote free and fair 2023 elections in the DRC through countering disinformation and hate speech and ensuring public access to accurate information...FY 2022 funds will support the protection and defense of journalists under threat and strengthen the legal framework to enable free media, open information access, and freedom of expression. Key interventions will strengthen advocacy capacity, digital and physical security awareness, response capabilities, and media networking activities. USAID will promote positive, nonviolent male development to shift attitudes and practices among boys and youth, including a focus on child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and gender-based violence (GBV)...MSDA contributes to Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by promoting responsive, transparent, and accountable public institutions in the DRC and improving their respect for human rights and basic freedoms through the support of free press..In addition, $250,000 for this IM will meet the control for the Gender Equity and Equality Action (GEEA) Fund. Programming will align with Priority 5: Dismantle Systemic Gender Barriers. USAID will provide robust capacity building for female journalists and women-led media associations to promote critical conversations and create a safe, democratic space for dialogue on women's and girls' issues.. .
